chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed the obligatory circumambulation (Tawaf), then became ill with an ailment that prevented him from completing the Tawaf. He (peace be upon him) said: If he had performed four circuits, he should instruct someone to perform three circuits on his behalf; thus his Tawaf is complete. And if he had performed three circuits and was unable to perform the Tawaf, then this is from what Allah has overcome him with, so there is no harm if he delays the Tawaf for one day and two days.

So if the illness leaves him, he returns and performs seven (circuits). And if his illness prolongs, he should instruct someone to perform seven (circuits) on his behalf, and he himself prays two cycles, and someone performs Sa'i on his behalf, and he has exited his Ihram. And similarly he does regarding the Sa'i and regarding the pelting of the Jamarat.

key_terms.رَمْيِ الْجِمَار: Pelting of the Jamarat (stoning of the devil)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who becomes ill and cannot complete the obligatory Tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the juristic distinctions for a pilgrim incapacitated during Tawaf, emphasizing the principle of *al-ghalabah* (dominance of difficulty) to relieve obligation. It establishes that while minor illness permits delaying to complete the circuits, prolonged incapacity allows for proxy performance (*tafwid*), thereby permitting the pilgrim to exit the state of Ihram, a ruling extended by scholars to Sa'i and Rami.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Is’haq Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws regarding a man who circumambulated the Obligatory Tawaaf. Then becomes unwell with such an illness that he is unable, along with it, upon completing the Tawaaf. So heasws said: ‘If he had performed four circuits, he can instruct someone to perform three circuits on his behalf; and if he had performed three circuits, and he was not able upon the Tawaaf, so this one is from the one whom Allahazwj has Overcome upon. Therefore, there is no problem if he was to delay the Tawaaf for a day, and two days.

So if his illness leaves him, he would repeat, and he would perform seven (circuits). But, if his illness prolongs, he can instruct someone to perform Tawaaf on his behalf, seven (circuits), and he would Pray two Cycles, and perform Sa’ee on his behalf, and he would have come out from his Ihraam. And similar to that he would do regarding the Sa’ee, and regarding the pelting of the rocks’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who performs obligatory Tawaf then something happens, because of which he cannot complete. He (the Imam) said, Tf he has performed four times Tawaf (walking around the House) he can appoint someone to complete the other three times Tawaf (walking around the House) for him, and his Tawaf is complete. If he has performed three times Tawaf (walking around the House) and cannot do any more, he then is one whom Allah has overpowered and it is not harmful to delay his Tawaf by one or two days.

If his problem goes away, he comes to complete his seven times Tawaf (walking around the House); if his problem prolongs he appoints someone to perform for him seven times Tawaf (walking around the House), two Rak‘at Salat (prayer) and Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah and he then comes out of the state of Ihram. He can follow the same procedure in Sa‘y and throwing pebbles (Ramy al-Jamarat).”’
